purpose: Pre-recovery baseline. Recovery is measured by movement in these bucket counts and by the 18-URL cohort's index status -- NOT by a GSC 'validation passed' badge.

exportSamples.note: GSC caps drilldown exports at 1,000 rows. All percentages below are EXTRAPOLATIONS from a 1,000-URL sample, not exact counts of the full bucket.

soft404.interpretation: ~75% appears to be recoverable outage damage; ~25% the intentional fail-closed state. EXTRAPOLATED from 1,000 of 2,924.

crawledNotIndexed.interpretation: ~65% thin /naics + /agencies sub-pages at ~400 words. Separate defect, deferred until after the recovery window.

entries.note: Resubmitted 2026-08-25 as recovery step 3. This is the one robots.txt declares.
STALE - not read since 2026-07-17, three days before the July 20 breakpoint. Also a DUPLICATE registration: this file is already a child of sitemap-index.xml, so Google holds it twice.

observations: Discovered pages 37,640 exceeds the 35,309 URLs the live sitemap currently emits. Both rows report the same 37,640, consistent with a cached/aggregate figure rather than a fresh per-sitemap count.

The standalone sitemap.xml last-read date (2026-07-17) is the closest July-side timing signal found so far. It is NOT proof of causation - a stale last-read may be a symptom of reduced crawl attention rather than its cause.

step3_resubmitSitemap.what: sitemap-index.xml resubmitted, read same day, Success

step4_cohortIndexing.what: Request Indexing attempted for the 18-URL cohort, ordered TOP -> MIDDLE -> DEEP by July impressions.
step4_cohortIndexing.outcome: Google capped the submissions ("quota exceeded"). The exact count accepted before the cap was not recorded.
step4_cohortIndexing.implication: The cohort is now SPLIT into requested and not-requested subsets, and we do not know the boundary. This weakens it as a controlled sample: a URL that recovers may have been manually requested or may have recovered on its own via the Aug 25 sitemap read.
step4_cohortIndexing.mitigation: Sitemap resubmission (step 3) covers ALL 9,437 /contracts URLs regardless of manual requests. Bucket-count movement remains the primary measure; the cohort is now supporting evidence, not the controlled arm.
step4_cohortIndexing.nextAction: Do NOT re-request tomorrow. Instead record each cohort URL's coverage status + last crawl date via URL Inspection (read-only, no quota), which is what step 5 actually needs.

step5_recordCohortStatus.what: For each of the 18: coverage status (Indexed / Crawled-not-indexed / Not found / Unknown) + last crawl date.
step5_recordCohortStatus.note: URL Inspection READ is not quota-limited; only Request Indexing is. Status can be captured for all 18 today.

validateFix.why: GSC validates the whole issue category; both buckets contain intentional exclusions (~680 valid 404s, ~25% fail-closed Soft 404s), so validation would fail even while recovery works.
